title: Consolidate enterprise client patterns: token rotation, service-account UX, and stream restart semantics
creator: Anika Rao
description: Summary: Multiple enterprise customers have submitted distinct requests that surface a common scaffolding gap in our client libraries: (1) ergonomics for long-lived streaming connections (resume/reconnect semantics and backpressure), (2) clear service-account and token-rotation patterns for automated CI/CD and platform integrations, and (3) consistent language-level support for Go and Rust client idioms. These requests are not bugs but feature/UX gaps that impede enterprise adoption for Dedicated/Private deployments. Goal: define a consolidated set of client primitives, docs, and minimal API/contract changes that allows teams to implement secure token rotation, resumable streams, and idiomatic clients across 3 prioritized languages (Python, Go, Rust) with clear upgrade and rollout plans.
acceptance_criteria: Public design doc with proposed client primitives and API surface published and reviewed by Eng/Design/SEC
Design prototypes for stream resume tokens and backpressure semantics (sequence numbers + optional checkpoint API) validated in integration tests
Auth pattern cookbook (service-account key rotation, short-lived tokens, recommended refresh cadence) added to SDK docs
Minimum viable Go and Rust examples implemented in the monorepo examples/ folder and passing CI smoke tests against a staging Dedicated instance
Runbook for rolling SDK changes with backward-compatible server behavior documented for Private customers
decisions: Adopt a resume-token approach for streaming: server issues opaque resume_token on each acknowledged checkpoint; clients may reconnect with resume_token to resume KV caches up to last acknowledged token
Introduce "client-refresh" sample in SDKs to model token rotation (obtain new access token via service account exchange) rather than building KMS integrations into the SDK core
Prioritize Go ergonomics first for low-level streaming primitives (goroutine-safe connectors), then Rust for performance-sensitive customers, Python remains maintenance-first
tradeoffs: Resume tokens increase server state bookkeeping and slightly higher metadata per-stream, but reduce duplicate work for long-running streams (net positive for enterprise telemetry workloads)
Exposing token-rotation helpers in SDK keeps common patterns simple but risks diverging implementations; we mitigate via small, well-reviewed helper APIs and canonical examples
Full automatic KMS key rotation in SDKs postponed to 2nd phase to reduce initial surface area and security review time
next_steps: Draft public design doc in Drive and assign Eng/SEC reviewers (owner: Diego Martinez)
Create engineering spike ticket in ENG board to prototype resume_token flow against staging runtime (owner: Priya Kapoor)
Add two example clients to monorepo: examples/sdk-go-stream-resume and examples/sdk-rust-token-rotation (owners: Eng SDK team)
Prep a short rollout note for Customer Success with mitigation steps for Private customers who cannot upgrade servers immediately
comments: 2026-01-19 - Diego Martinez: Initial intake call notes with Acme Corp and FinData: both asked for resumable streaming and sample code for automated token rotation in CI. They flagged auditability and short-lived tokens as must-haves.

2026-01-22 - Priya Kapoor (Eng): Spike accepted; Eng will prototype resume_token and a lightweight checkpoint API. Plan to keep server-side state minimal by encoding checkpoint metadata into resume_token payload.

2026-01-28 - Security review (SEC): Preliminary feedback requested stronger guidance around refresh token storage patterns for on-prem agents; recommended we include a security appendix in the cookbook.
2026-01-30 - Design review (Maya Chen): UX asks for explicit reconnection timeline in examples and failure semantics for partial messages; proposed API adds on_reconnect callback and backoff hooks.

2026-02-02 - PM update: Consolidated doc moved to 'Design review' stage; next is Eng spike kickoff and creation of example repos. Customer Success looped in to validate acceptance criteria with pilot customers.
